newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig managers seek board backing - union.
newsitem.headline: Grundig managers seek board backing - union.

text.p: Executives at crisis-hit German consumer electronics maker Grundig AG will seek a vote of confidence from the company's supervisory board at a meeting next Monday, the IG Metall union said on Thursday.
IG Metall, which represents staff on the company's works council, also called for the Bavarian state government to take over temporary control of Grundig and put together a rescue consortium.

IG Metall representative Gerd Lobodda told a news conference that Grundig chief executive Pieter van der Wal and supervisory board chief Christian Schwarz-Schilling would be seeking the backing of the supervisory board at the meeting.
He also called on the Bavarian state government to try and build a consortium made up of regional banks and at least two powerful industrial companies to turn around Grundig.
He named Siemens AG as one potential candidate to strengthen Grundig's management.
"At the moment, we haven't the slightest idea who is really running Grundig," Lobodda told reporters.

"Our main goal must be not to cause any further concern among suppliers and creditors, otherwise there could be a chain reaction which could mean the end of an otherwise financially solid business," he added.
Loss-making Grundig tipped into crisis after Dutch Philips NV recently said it was pulling out of management control over the company and would adopt a role as a passive shareholder.
Finance director Karl Heinz Wieland quit his post last week.
IG Metall has said it lost confidence in management after Van der Wal announced plans to cut the workforce to 6,000 from 8,500 now by the turn of the century.
